data.narrative:
Emerald AI is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Varun Sivaram that has raised $68M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 9 peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including 8 private companies (Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen among them) and 1 public company (LNZA).

Due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum density thresholds (fewer than 3 datapoints in narrow filters), the Peer-Median method is not applicable. This limitation reflects the current sparsity of comparable seed-stage climate-tech valuations. The Stage-Progression method is applicable and uses a standard 2.5x multiplier for the Seed-to-next-stage transition, anchored to the $68M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $170M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $144M to $195M, with $170M as the median point. This narrow one-method triangulation carries material execution risk: the estimate depends entirely on typical stage-progression patterns in the sector, without independent peer-based validation. Key uncertainties include (1) whether Emerald AI's metrics and progress align with the typical Seed-stage cohort; (2) whether the 2.5x multiplier reflects current market conditions in climate tech; and (3) the absence of comparable-company checks to ground the stage-progression assumption. A fuller valuation framework would require either identifying additional narrowly comparable seed-stage peers or conducting revenue/milestone-based scenarios.
